title: Week of Sep 21 - Sep 27
subtitle: Bridge week, not Block 4 week 1. You lost Thursday through Sunday to an infection and just started antibiotics, so this is a graded re-entry: loads at 70 to 85% of your recent tops, every set 4 or more in reserve, 17 easy miles, no quality run, no failure sets. Block 4 slides one week to Sep 28 and the whole calendar moves with it, same as the August road trip. The research behind the shape of it is in the goals below.
goals: What this week is. You logged Monday and Wednesday, ran the time trial Tuesday at 21:44 with the illness already coming on, ran 1.7 easy Thursday, then lost Friday, Saturday and Sunday. That is about four full days off and a 9.5 mile week against a planned 20. Block 4 now starts Sep 28. TRAINING_CYCLE is already updated, including the bench track dates and the mileage ramp.

What the week off actually cost, because this drives everything else. Strength: nothing worth planning around. Trained lifters hold maximal strength through two full weeks without training (Hwang 2017, JSCR), and 3 to 5 days of cessation after a hard block leaves it equal or better (Pritchard 2018, JSCR). Aerobic: small but real. VO2max falls about 7% after 10 days off and 4 to 5% after 14 (Coyle 1984, Houmard 1992), so four days is maybe 2%. What you will actually feel is blood plasma, which drops about 5% in two weeks and takes heart rate up several beats at the same pace. Expect easy runs to read 5 to 10 beats high this week at your normal effort. That is fluid, not fitness, and it refills within about a week of normal training. So the plan is not rebuilt, it restarts one notch down.

How the first two sessions are built. The IOC consensus on acute respiratory illness in athletes (Schwellnus 2022) uses a graded return with an exercise challenge at 60 to 70% of normal intensity, then checks symptoms during, right after, and 24 hours after. Monday is exactly that test: a light lower body session and 1.5 easy miles. If it holds overnight, Tuesday and Wednesday step up. The graded templates from the COVID era have the same shape (15 to 20 min under 70% max HR, then 30 min, then light lifting). Stop the session and the week for any of these: chest pain or tightness, racing or irregular heartbeat, breathlessness out of proportion to the effort, dizziness, or very dark urine.

Gates before Monday morning. No session if you have a fever now or had one in the last 24 hours, or if symptoms are below the neck (chest cough, body aches, real fatigue). Fever plus exercise is the myocarditis case and it is the one that actually matters. Fever also raises oxygen cost about 13% per degree C, so the session is garbage anyway. Any of that and Monday becomes a 20 minute walk and everything slides two days. If this was strep, CDC puts you past meaningful contagiousness after 12 hours on antibiotics with no fever, which is the gym question.

Lifting. Everything at 70 to 85% of your recent tops, one top set, 4 or more in reserve, no grinding anywhere. Monday squat 175x5 (78% of the 225 triples you actually did last Monday) and RDL 155x8. Wednesday bench ramps to 185x3 (you did 195 doubles on the 16th and called them controlled) and OHP 110x5. Friday deadlift 255x3 (85% of the 300x4) and paused bench 150x4. Saturday pull-ups are 3x8 submax, no max set anywhere this week, the fresh-day max series restarts Oct 3 from 19. 69 planned sets, the same count as the deload, at much lighter loads. Frequency and movement, not stimulus.

Running. 17 miles, all easy, no quality touch. Tue 3, Thu 3.5, Sat 4, Sun 2.5, plus short jogs after the three lifts. Cap is 145 Monday through Wednesday and 150 from Thursday, and if the number runs high at an easy effort, hold the effort and let the number be high. Saturday long run debuts next week at 6 miles. Block 4 mileage becomes 22, 25, 27 with a 19 mile deload instead of 25, 26, 28, which keeps the 7 day to 28 day load ratio under 1.4 the whole way through the block.

Bench 225 track, shifted one week, nothing else changed. Sep 28 week ramps to 205x2 with 2x4 at 180. Oct 5 week is 215x1 then 2x3 at 190. The attempt is Wednesday Oct 14, retry Oct 21. This week's Wednesday 185x3 and Friday paused 150x4 are the placeholders, well under both. Safety arms at chest height before the first set, as always.

Food and the scale. Eat at maintenance this week rather than the 400 deficit. Recovery from an infection and re-entry to training both run better fed, and your logging stopped Wednesday anyway, so restart full day logging with the deficit at zero and put it back to 400 when Block 4 starts Sep 28. The scale will read low from four days of eating almost nothing and then jump back up. Ignore both readings. Waist Sunday morning as usual.

The morning routine is the real task Monday. The habit research is on your side here: automaticity takes about 66 days to build but missing a few days does not undo it, the gains resume after a missed performance (Gardner, Lally and Wardle 2012). What carries it is the cue, so keep the same alarm, the same clothes laid out the night before, the same gym, the same start time, and make the session small enough that showing up is the only hard part. Do not try to win the week back on Monday.
review: Deload week Sep 14 to 20, cut short by the illness. Monday you went past the deload script to 225 squats ("collapsing a little bit and having to very intentionally hold my knees out, but it felt good to push myself like that") and RDL 225x5. Tuesday the 5K time trial: 3.14 miles in 21:44 at 184 average, over the sub-21:00 gate, and the illness arrived the same day, so that is a floor and not a verdict. Wednesday you ramped bench to 195 doubles, "195 didn't exactly feel easy but very controlled, way more than last week", plus OHP 125 and pull-ups 2x10. Thursday was 1.7 easy miles at 135, and that was the end of it. Friday's deadlifts, Saturday's calisthenics and Sunday's 5 miles all gone. 36 of 69 planned sets, 9.5 of 20 miles. Block 3 still closes with every Block 1 best beaten.
